hints.limitIntro: Limit per value for string, bytes in UTF-8, umlauts count twice:

limitRows.indexedReason: the value is a term in the index, Lucene rejects longer terms when writing (“immense term”), the whole document fails
limitRows.docValuesReason: the column for strings has the same limit
limitRows.storedOnlyReason: the value only lives in the document, which may be large, the limit is the request size

indexed.title: indexed: the field goes into the search index
paragraphs: The index runs from value to document: for every term it lists the documents it occurs in. That is finding and filtering, “which documents have 4711”. Only an indexed field can be searched, filtered (fq) and used for facets.
Switched off, the value is only stored and returned with the document, but no query finds it. Example: the path on the file store, which is only there to look up.
Effect: every indexed field makes the index bigger and writing slower, for texts noticeably. Switching it on later only affects new documents, old ones stay invisible until the core is rebuilt.
Counterpart: docValues run the other way, from document to value. Whoever filters and sorts needs both.

stored.title: stored: the original value stays in the document
paragraphs: A stored field comes back with a query (fl). Switched off, the value is only searchable but never readable again.

For us all real fields are stored, because Solr is the only storage for these cores: only then can a core be rebuilt from itself. Atomic updates also need stored or docValues for every field, otherwise the document loses values on a partial update.
Large full texts cost space but stay stored. Result lists simply do not request them.

multiValued.title: multiValued: several values per document
paragraphs: The field may carry a list per document, e.g. several article numbers on a data sheet. The search hits every value, facets count every value.
Consequences: the field cannot be sorted by, and it cannot provide the ID of the document.
Switching it later means rebuilding the core, Solr does not rewrite old documents.

docValues.title: docValues: a column-wise copy of the values
paragraphs: docValues run from document to value: for every document its value sits in a continuous column, like in a table. That is not for finding, the index is already the fastest structure for that. It is for the questions afterwards: once the hits are known, you want to sort, count or calculate with their value, and for that Solr must look up per hit which value this document has. The index cannot do that, it only runs the other way.

Sorting, facets, grouping and functions like the recency boost run fast over docValues and without memory for the field cache. Without docValues Solr would have to invert the index and keep the result in memory: slow the first time, and it eats memory.
Costs disk space. Only works for string, long, double, date and boolean, not for text.
What for: every field that is sorted or counted by, e.g. status, file sub class, date. Whoever also filters by it needs indexed as well: two lists in opposite directions.

required.title: required: no document without a value
paragraphs: Solr rejects every document missing the value, with an error when writing. For mandatory fields like id.
Careful when adding it later: old documents without the value can only be written again once they get the value, even on a partial update.

suggest.title: suggest: a twin for completion while typing
paragraphs: Creates the field <name>Suggested, which stores every value as prefixes from 3 characters (EdgeNGram). Solr fills it itself via copyField, no code writes it. It drives the suggestions while typing and the filter offers of the search, the field itself stays exact.
Word by word for texts, on the whole value for string, long and double. Not for boolean and date.
Costs index space: all prefixes of every value. The twin is never stored and does not appear in this table.

type.title: Type: the fieldType in the base schema
paragraphs: string: the value as it comes, not split, not lower-cased. Only matches exactly. For keys, status, numbers, hashes. The whole value is one term, and a term may have at most 32766 bytes: this applies with indexed and with docValues, umlauts count twice. Stored only (both off), a string may be arbitrarily large, like a preview image.

long: whole number with 64 bits, for ranges and sorting. There is no int, whole numbers are always long for us. double: decimal number with 64 bits. date: point in time per ISO 8601 in UTC, for ranges and sorting. boolean: true or false.

text_minimal: split at spaces, all lower case. Punctuation stays on the token, so a file name stays hittable word by word. text_word: also split at punctuation (StandardTokenizer), all lower case, for descriptions and multilingual JSON. text_words: takes finished tokens from the backend, which stems and splits compounds beforehand, Solr only compares. Every search must prepare its input the same way. For all text types the term limit applies per token, the value itself may be arbitrarily large.
Changing a type later means rebuilding the core, Solr does not rewrite old documents.

id.title: ID: the primary key of the core
paragraphs: The key marks id, the primary key of every core (uniqueKey in Solr). Solr does not allow changing it after the core is created, so it is called id everywhere, comes with every core by itself and is fixed: string, indexed, required, never multiValued, not deletable. stored, docValues, description and position are free.
What goes in is described in the description of the field, e.g. the hash of the bytes (sha256) for the DMS. Whoever fills the core follows that. Solr rejects documents without id.
